m:duomo: The cathedral is free and open Monday to Saturday, 10:15am–3:45pm; it can't be visited on Sundays (from guides: to be confirmed). Shoulders and knees covered. To climb the dome (463 steps) or the bell tower you need a separate ticket, with a time slot for the dome: see the full visit on another day.
m:cupola: The Brunelleschi Pass costs €30 and is valid for 3 days: it includes the dome, bell tower, Baptistery, museum and crypt, each once. For the dome you must book a time (on the pass's first day) and bring ID: it's 463 steps with no lift. Dome: Monday–Friday 8:15am–6:45pm, Saturday until 4:30pm, Sunday 12:45–4:30pm. The bell tower (414 steps) is closed from 9 to 13 November 2026 for maintenance. The museum is closed on the first Tuesday of the month. Hours and price from guides updated in 2026: confirm on duomo.firenze.it.
m:signoria: The square is free. Inside Palazzo Vecchio the museum costs €18 and the Arnolfo Tower €20 (prices from 1 February 2026, City of Florence). It's usually open 9am–7pm, on Thursdays it closes at 2pm (from guides: to be confirmed). The historic cafés around the square are expensive: drink at the counter.
m:uffizi: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 8:15am–6:30pm (ticket office until 5:30pm), closed on Mondays. Booking is strongly recommended: full ticket €25, plus €4 booking fee (cultura.gov.it; the price drops in low-season months, check uffizi.it). On the first Sunday of the month entry is free but without booking, with very long queues.
m:accademia: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 8:15am–6:50pm (last entry about 6:20pm), closed on Mondays. The full ticket costs €20 from 1 February 2026, plus about €4 if you book a time (recommended). Arrive at least 15 minutes before your slot: if you're late you lose the booking. On the first Sunday of the month it's free but you can't book.
m:pontevecchio: Free to cross at any hour. The jewellery shops open during the day and usually close on Sundays and public holidays.
m:santacroce: Ticket €8 (basilica, museum, cloisters and Pazzi Chapel). Open Monday–Saturday 9:30am–5:30pm, Sunday and holidays 2–5:30pm (from guides, March 2026: to be confirmed). Shoulders and knees covered.
m:smn: Ticket €7.50 (basilica, Avelli cemetery and museum). From October to March usually 9am–5:30pm (from guides, March 2026; Friday and Sunday hours may differ: check smn.it). Shoulders and knees covered.
m:piazzale: The piazzale is free and always open. San Miniato is free: usually 9:30am–1pm and 3–7pm (from guides: to be confirmed), with the monks' Gregorian-chant vespers around 5:30pm on weekdays. Take bus 12 or 13, or walk: the climb takes about 30 minutes.
m:pitti: The garden costs €10 (€13 if you book ahead). It's closed on the first and last Monday of every month; it closes at 5:30pm from 25 October (winter time) and at 4:30pm in November. Tickets for Palazzo Pitti and its galleries are separate: check prices on uffizi.it.
m:sanlorenzo: The ground floor of the Mercato Centrale is open Monday to Saturday, about 9am–3pm, closed on Sundays; the first floor (food hall) is open every day until the evening. The outdoor leather stalls are closed on Mondays (from guides). The Medici Chapels cost €11 (from 1 February 2026), open Tuesday to Sunday 8:15am–6:50pm (to be confirmed).
m:santospirito: The square and the workshops are free to see. During the day many artisans work with their doors open, but on Monday mornings and Sundays several workshops are closed.
vd:gilli: A historic café founded in 1733 on Piazza della Repubblica: marble, mirrors and cases of pastries. For breakfast have a cappuccino and cornetto at the counter: it costs much less than at a table.
vp:gilli: At the counter breakfast is about €5–7; at a table much more (menu not seen, to be confirmed).
vd:rivoire: The historic café facing Palazzo Vecchio, open since 1872: the thick hot chocolate is the speciality. Closed on Mondays.
vp:rivoire: At the counter a coffee or hot chocolate costs little; sitting on the square costs much more (menu not seen, to be confirmed).
vd:nerbone: The historic counter inside the Mercato Centrale, running since 1872: a lampredotto sandwich (beef tripe with green sauce) or boiled beef, eaten standing among the crowd. Closed on Sundays.
vp:nerbone: Budget: a sandwich costs a few euros (hours from guides, which give opening at 7 or 8am; to be confirmed).
vd:mercatocentrale: The first floor of the San Lorenzo market, a hall with many stalls: pizza, trapizzino, truffle and Tuscan cooking under one roof. Useful when you can't agree on what to eat.
vp:mercatocentrale: It costs more than real trattorias: for example truffle tagliolini cost about €20, pizza and sandwiches much less (from guides, to be confirmed).
vd:trmario: A family trattoria near the Mercato Centrale, open only at lunch, with shared tables: ribollita, pasta, tripe and steak. Cash only and no bookings. Closed on Sundays.
vp:trmario: Budget for Florence (menu not seen; hours and cash to be confirmed).
vd:gozzi: An old-fashioned trattoria opposite the basilica of San Lorenzo, open at lunch: Tuscan home cooking like ribollita, boiled meats and dishes of the day. Closed on Sundays.
vp:gozzi: Budget (menu not seen; hours to be confirmed).
vd:santambrogio: The Florentines' market, away from the crowds in the centre: fruit, cheeses, bread and, inside, the Da Rocco trattoria with local cooking at low prices. Closed on Sundays.
vp:santambrogio: Budget (market hours from guides; the trattoria's hours weren't checked).
vd:pizzaiuolo: A Neapolitan pizzeria much loved by Florentines, near the Sant'Ambrogio market: round pizza with soft dough and starters. It fills up early: best to book. Closed on Sundays.
vp:pizzaiuolo: A pizza and a drink stay around €15 (prices not seen, to be confirmed).
vd:casalinga: A trattoria with Tuscan home cooking near Piazza Santo Spirito, with close tables: ribollita, pappa al pomodoro, pasta, roasts. Closed on Sundays.
vp:casalinga: Low to mid-range: a meal with a pasta course and water is around €15–20 (prices not seen, to be confirmed).
vd:gustapizza: Cheap Neapolitan pizza on Via Maggio, a short walk from Palazzo Pitti and Santo Spirito: a small place, with a queue. Closed on Mondays.
vp:gustapizza: A pizza is under €10 (menu not seen, to be confirmed).
vd:vivoli: One of Florence's oldest gelaterias, a few steps from Santa Croce: artisan gelato in a cup or cone, with classic flavours. Closed on Mondays.
vp:vivoli: A small cup costs a few euros (menu not seen, to be confirmed).
vd:neri: An artisan gelateria on a narrow street behind the Uffizi, between Santa Croce and Piazza della Signoria: fruit and chocolate flavours, open until late.
vp:neri: A cup or cone costs a few euros (menu not seen, to be confirmed).
cd:bargello: Donatello's David and Michelangelo's sculptures in a medieval palace.
cx:bargello: State museum hours vary by day: check the website.
cd:palazzovecchio: The Hall of the Five Hundred and the Medici apartments, with the panoramic tower.
cd:medicee: Michelangelo's New Sacristy and the Medici tombs.
cx:medicee: State museum hours vary by day: check the website.
cd:sanmarco: Fra Angelico's frescoes in the cells of the Dominican convent.
cx:sanmarco: State museum hours vary by day: check the website.
cd:galileo: Galileo's scientific instruments and telescopes, near the Uffizi.
cd:strozzi: Temporary exhibitions in a Renaissance palace.
cd:bardini: A terraced garden in the Oltrarno, with one of the best views of the city.
cn:laurenziana: Basilica of San Lorenzo and Laurentian Library
cd:laurenziana: Brunelleschi's church and Michelangelo's staircase for the library.
cd:brancacci: Masaccio's frescoes that ushered in the Renaissance.
cd:ferragamo: Shoes of 20th-century stars in a palazzo on Piazza Santa Trinita.
